official.description_text:
Postdoctoral position in techno-economic analysis of resilient urban energy systems
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Industrial Engineering and Management
Do you want to develop and evaluate concepts for how a brand-new urban district can be supplied with both heat and electricity robustly, even when something unexpected happens, and see your analyses used as decision support by the municipality that will build it? Welcome with your application.
The position is part of a collaboration between KTH, Uppsala University and Uppsala Municipality on the energy system in Uppsala’s south-eastern districts. This is one of Sweden’s largest urban development projects, with 21,500 homes planned by 2050. You will work on a real question in a live setting, where your results directly affect how a district is built.
Two postdocs
are being recruited in parallel to work closely together:
one at KTH
(this position) and
one at Uppsala University. Part of the working time is spent at Uppsala Municipality
, which gives direct access to planning documentation, stakeholders and the questions that are current during implementation. The project is part of the research area STandUP for Energy.
Job description
The position aims to generate and evaluate concepts for the energy supply of Uppsala’s south-eastern districts, and to analyse them techno-economically as decision support for the municipality.
Duties include:
developing, modelling and comparing concepts for a flexible low-temperature heating system
techno-economically evaluating a flexible electricity microgrid
analysing the heating system and the electricity microgrid as an integrated multi-energy system
quantifying the socio-economic value of the energy system’s resilience
analysing the security of supply of the heat and electricity systems during disruptions, and how concept and sizing choices affect recovery time and outage costs
developing scenarios for the district’s build-out, connection rates, energy demand, technology rollout and system configuration
carrying out techno-economic analyses of the integrated system
analysing business models and implementation models for both systems
translating the results into decision support
publishing results in scientific journals and presenting them at conferences
taking part in applications for external research funding, nationally and within the EU
Qualifications
Requirements
A PhD in energy technology, energy systems, mechanical engineering or equivalent, or a foreign degree deemed equivalent. The degree must be completed no later than when the employment decision is made.
Documented experience of modelling, optimization and analysis of energy systems, preferably integrated or multi-energy systems
Experience of techno-economic analysis, investment planning, infrastructure sizing or operational optimization
Knowledge of thermal energy systems, for example district heating, heat pumps or thermal storage
Understanding of energy markets and policy instruments, for both heat and electricity
Programming skills and experience developing or applying computational models for energy system analysis
The ability to express yourself in English, orally and in writing, as English is used daily in the project
Personal skills
Good collaboration skills and the ability to communicate research results to stakeholders outside academia
Goal-oriented and self-driven approach to work
Preferred qualification
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience in low-temperature heating systems, waste heat recovery, thermal storage or other distributed energy resources
Experience in modelling, optimization or sector coupling of integrated energy systems
Experience in resilience or reliability analysis of energy systems, security of supply, or valuation of outage costs
Experience in energy economics/business models, or collaboration with municipalities, authorities or industry
Commitment to and awareness of gender equality, diversity, and equal opportunities.
knowledge of Swedish, or willingness to learn it, for the work with the municipality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.
Trade union representatives
Contact information to
trade union representatives.
To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.
A
position as a postdoctoral fellow
is a time-limited qualified appointment focusing mainly on research, intended as a first career step after a dissertation.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position at KTH developing techno-economic models and analysis of integrated energy systems (heating and electricity) for a real urban development project in Uppsala. The role combines systems modelling, optimization, energy economics, and stakeholder communication with direct municipal decision support.

thematic_fit.rationale: The researcher's thematic focus is human-centred immersive systems, collaborative learning, spatial cognition, and wayfinding — none present in this energy systems engineering role. Urban energy infrastructure planning and resilience analysis are entirely outside the researcher's domain. The position is grounded in mechanical engineering, energy technology, and infrastructure economics, not HCI or immersive design.

methodological_fit.rationale: The position emphasizes systems modelling, optimization, techno-economic analysis, and computational energy system models. The researcher has beginner Python and intermediate quantitative research experience, but no demonstrated experience with energy system optimization, modelling infrastructure, investment planning, or multi-energy systems. The required programming depth (developing/applying computational models for energy analysis) substantially exceeds the researcher's current Python competency. The methodological approach (engineering optimization) differs from the researcher's empirical human-centred evaluation methods.

growth_value.rationale: This position would develop systems-level thinking and advanced Python/modelling skills, but neither advances toward the target identity. Energy systems expertise does not close gaps in spatial cognition research, immersive system design, or human-centred evaluation methodologies. The role offers no pathway to developing human-centred XR research leadership.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is well-regarded and located in a preferred country (Sweden). The position involves real-world impact and stakeholder engagement, which could strengthen communication skills. However, the research direction (energy infrastructure) is orthogonal to the target identity. The collaboration with Uppsala Municipality and direct policy impact, while valuable, does not support building a trajectory toward human-centred immersive systems research or preparing for group leadership in HCI/XR.

eligibility_flags: Position requires a completed PhD in energy technology, energy systems, mechanical engineering, or equivalent; researcher currently holds MSc by Research in progress. Eligibility depends on PhD completion by employment decision date.
Posting mentions security clearance requirement under Swedish Protective Security Act (2018:585) for unspecified positions; ambiguous whether this specific role is classified as security-sensitive.
Documented experience in energy system modelling, optimization, and techno-economic analysis is required. Researcher has no demonstrated background in energy systems or infrastructure modelling.
risks: Complete thematic misalignment. Energy infrastructure is not part of the researcher's target research identity.
Researcher lacks documented experience in energy systems, optimization methods, district heating, thermal storage, energy markets, and infrastructure planning — all core requirements.
Taking a postdoc in energy systems would further distance the researcher from developing expertise and networks in human-centred XR/HCI research.
Beginner Python is below the competency level needed for developing computational energy models. Steep learning curve would delay project contribution.
Position's mentorship and group leadership development pathways would build expertise in energy engineering, not HCI or immersive systems research leadership.
